issues.title: Poisson potential theorem lacks boundary regularity

failure_location.quote: where $\Phi(x,y)$ is the fundamental solution of the Laplace equation, $n_y$ is the outward pointing normal vector to $y$

issues.failure_explanation: BIM is stated under the standing assumption that Ω is only a compact domain and quantifies the representation and trace over its boundary. An admissible nonsmooth boundary need not have a pointwise outward normal at every boundary point, so the normal derivative and the asserted pointwise one-half jump/BIE contract are not available as stated. The new C2 condition supplies a setting in which those boundary objects are well-defined.
issues.overall_effect: The potential representation and all PFNN results that invoke its pointwise boundary trace are unsupported for the full arbitrary-compact-geometry scope claimed in the old version.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Adopt a common hypothesis that Ω is a bounded domain with C² boundary in BIM and every listed dependent result, and limit the arbitrary-geometry prose to that class. Under this hypothesis the pointwise normal derivative and one-half interior jump can be used, while the existing representations, method, and error rates remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: This is a contained hypothesis repair rather than new proof architecture, and the full chain survives for a broad smooth-domain class. It exceeds minor severity because the old source expressly allowed arbitrary compact geometries, while C² regularity excludes natural and widely used nonsmooth domains such as polygons. The surviving smooth-domain results are nevertheless recognizably comparable, so the loss is limited rather than major.

issues.title: FNN weights omit the Krasnoselskii–Mann relaxation factor

diagnostic_evidence.quote: since in the Fredholm NN we consider constant values for the parameter in the Krasnoselskii-Mann iteration, $\kappa_{\nu} = \kappa$

issues.failure_explanation: At a grid node the old matrix implements (1−κ)f_i+Σ_j K_ij f_jΔz+κg_i. The relaxed fixed-point step for the stated operator is (1−κ)f_i+κΣ_j K_ij f_jΔz+κg_i. Unless κ=1, the old network therefore has a different update and generally a different fixed point from the integral equation it claims to approximate.
issues.overall_effect: The constructed FNN, and hence each PFNN that uses it to obtain the boundary density, does not implement the advertised KM iteration for general κ; its convergence and error claims are consequently unsupported for the printed matrices.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Multiply every quadrature-kernel coefficient in the hidden and final FNN matrices by κ, including setting K_D(z)=κK(z,z)Δz+(1−κ). Verify nodewise that each corrected layer performs (1−κ)f+κ(g+K_Nf), and invoke the listed PFNN convergence and error results only for these corrected matrices.
issues.why_classification: The printed matrices define a coherent but incorrect iteration, so this is not merely a transcriptional typo. Nevertheless, the KM formula uniquely supplies a short, routine, local correction; no new lemma or architecture is needed, and the intended fixed point, convergence guarantee, and affected chain are preserved without loss.

issues.title: Poisson PFNN uses a unit-disk construction under general geometry

failure_location.quote: where $x^*:= (1, \phi) \in \partial \Omega$ is the unique point on the boundary corresponding to $x:= (r, \phi) \in \Omega$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We note that the approaches developed are applicable to any type of geometry for the domain and corresponding boundary.
However, for the examples presented, we will be considering a 2D disc domain, with unit radius and the corresponding unit circle boundary.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition is presented under the paper's general-domain setup, but its proof only supports the unit disk: x*=(1,φ) need not lie on the boundary of another domain, and the value ∂Φ(x*,y)/∂n_y=1/(4π) was obtained from the unit-circle calculation. Thus the argument establishes a disk-specific construction rather than the advertised general-geometry result.
issues.overall_effect: The old Poisson PFNN formula is not executable as stated on a general geometry and its constant-kernel simplification gives the wrong final-layer data away from the unit circle.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For a general regular domain, retain the unspecialized potential identity already displayed before the unit-circle simplification. Specify a deterministic boundary selection p(x), using the nearest boundary point wherever it is unique and a stated tie-breaking selection otherwise, set x*=p(x), and use the actual kernel ∂Φ(x*,y)/∂n_y in the weights and bias. State that x*=(1,φ) and ∂Φ(x*,y)/∂n_y=1/(4π) apply only to the unit disk.
issues.why_classification: The general identity needed for this repair is already present in the old proof, so no new potential-theory argument or restriction to the disk is necessary. Correcting the boundary-point definition and confining the constant-kernel specialization are short and local while preserving the proposition's general-domain mathematical content. It is substantive rather than a typo because an executable geometric selection and scope correction are required.

issues.title: Helmholtz fundamental solution uses λ instead of √λ

failure_location.quote: Theorem \ref{BIM} holds for the PDE (\ref{helmholtz-pde}), however the fundamental solution changes, and we have $\Phi(x,y) = -\frac{1}{2 \pi} K_0(\lambda | x-y|),$ where $K_0$ is the modified Bessel function of the second kind (with index 0, in 2D space).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and is given by $\Phi(x,y) = -\frac{1}{2\pi} K_0\left( \sqrt{\lambda} |x - y| \right)$, where $K_0$ is the modified Bessel function of the second kind.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the fundamental solution for Δ−λ has Bessel argument λ|x−y|. The old paper's own proposition proof instead states and uses √λ|x−y| while asserting that this kernel satisfies LΦ=δ. These are different kernels for general λ, so the prose formula misstates the kernel actually established and used by the paper.
issues.overall_effect: A reader following the introductory formula would construct the wrong Helmholtz kernel for general λ, although the subsequent formal proof and numerical section already use the corrected scaling.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace K_0(λ|x−y|) in the introductory Helmholtz sentence by K_0(√λ|x−y|), leaving the surrounding claim unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The PDE Δ−λ, the proposition's proof, and the numerical section all independently and uniquely force the √λ scaling. The erroneous scaling occurs only in the prose formula, and correcting it requires no repair to any inference, construction, or guarantee.

issues.title: Helmholtz punctured-domain divergence calculation is invalid

failure_location.quote: 0 = \int_{\partial \Omega} \mathcal{L}\Phi(x,y) d\sigma_y = \int_{\Omega - B(x,\epsilon)} \Delta_y \Phi(x, y) dy - \lambda \int_{\partial B(x,\epsilon)} \frac{\partial \Phi(x,y)}{\partial n_y} d\sigma_y.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the fundamental solution of the linear operator $\mathcal{L} := \Delta - \lambda$ satisfies:

issues.failure_explanation: Away from the singular point, LΦ=0 must be integrated over Ω minus the puncturing ball. The −λ part is −λ times a volume integral of Φ; only the Laplacian term becomes boundary normal derivatives under the divergence theorem. Moreover, an inner semicircle contribution tending to −1/2 gives an outer-boundary contribution of +1/2 plus the volume term, not −1/2. The old displayed identities therefore do not establish the proposition's final potential representation.
issues.overall_effect: The Helmholtz final-layer representation lacks a valid derivation, so the PFNN error theorem and recurrent bound that use that representation are not established by the old proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the punctured-domain calculation by integrating (Δ_y−λ)Φ=0 over Ω minus the puncturing ball. After the divergence theorem, retain −λ times the volume integral of Φ and use inner-boundary flux limits −1 for an interior puncture and −1/2 for a boundary half-puncture. This gives the outer-boundary identities 1+λ∫_ΩΦ(x,y)dy and 1/2+λ∫_ΩΦ(x*,y)dy, respectively, and hence the stated coefficient 1/2+λ∫_ΩδΦ(x,y)dy. The listed error and recurrent bounds should invoke this corrected representation.
issues.why_classification: The old displayed calculation contains genuine invalid inferences and therefore is not a typo. However, the source already supplies all required ingredients—the equation away from the pole, the divergence theorem, and the local Bessel asymptotic—so the correction is a short, standard punctured-domain argument. It preserves the representation and every downstream guarantee without a new lemma or substantive weakening.

issues.title: Helmholtz output bias uses ΔΦ instead of δΦ
issues.failure_explanation: The formal construction states a bias involving the Laplacian ΔΦ, while immediately defining δΦ as the potential difference and proving a representation whose bias involves λδΦ. Thus the proof supports a different network weight from the proposition's printed statement; implementing ΔΦ literally changes the network output.
issues.overall_effect: The printed Helmholtz PFNN construction does not match the potential representation analyzed by the later error theorem, so a literal implementation has the wrong output bias.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ΔΦ by δΦ in the Helmholtz output-bias formula and in any copied occurrence of that bias in the dependent error calculation, using the already stated definition δΦ(x,y)=Φ(x,y)−Φ(x*,y).
issues.why_classification: The immediately following definition, the final potential representation, and the error-bound quantities uniquely force δΦ. The uppercase Δ is a transcriptional substitution for the already defined lowercase δ; no proof step or mathematical guarantee needs to change.

issues.title: FNN error estimate includes the undefined q=1 endpoint
issues.failure_explanation: The old hypothesis says that the operator is non-expansive, with the paper's preceding convention allowing q≤1. Its conclusion contains e^(1-q)/(1-q), which is undefined at the admissible value q=1. Thus the printed estimate supports only the stricter q<1 regime, not every operator admitted by the statement.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed explicit layer-dependent FNN estimate, and the downstream reference to that estimate in the PFNN error theorem, do not cover general non-expansive BIE operators at q=1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the blanket estimate by a two-case statement. Retain the displayed exponential estimate only for q<1. For q=1, state an explicit error-bound or metric-subregularity hypothesis for the affine fixed-point map and prove the corresponding KM estimate, for example a factor ρ^M with ρ=√(1−κ(1−κ)/μ²)<1 in the appropriate discretized Hilbert norm, including norm-conversion and quadrature terms. Amend the PFNN error theorem to invoke the applicable case and to carry the endpoint hypothesis; make no unqualified q=1 rate claim.
issues.why_classification: The singularity at q=1 is not removable: general non-expansive KM iterations need not possess the asserted uniform distance rate, and q=1 is a natural regime rather than an exceptional degeneracy. Thus a one-symbol restriction would surrender a substantive operator class. A contained split-case argument with an explicit endpoint regularity condition yields a recognizably comparable FNN and PFNN error chain without global reconstruction, making the issue moderate rather than serious.
